Walk me through how you redesigned the relay pipeline.

The old pipeline was purely serial: pull a batch, block on a ~204s safety timeout, generate proofs, submit to Supra, repeat. How do you handle Rust panics across the JNI boundary in Transmute?

All JNI functions are #[no_mangle] pub extern "system" — panics must not cross the JVM boundary. I use a throw! macro that converts all Rust errors to java/lang/RuntimeException via env.throw_new() and returns a safe fallback value. The release profile also uses panic = "abort", which removes unwinding tables entirely — this reduces binary size and eliminates a JNI safety concern by making panics unrecoverable rather than unwindable.

What async and concurrency model does Transmute use overall?

Four distinct layers. tokio with rt-multi-thread powers BatchProcessor, the CLI main, and compress_batch. rayon handles convert_batch, PDF image decode, and the JNI batchConvert. std::thread is used for the GUI background worker and ImageLoader — no tokio in the egui crate. pollster provides synchronous wrapping over wgpu async initialization and GPU readback. The boundary rule is that tokio::task::spawn_blocking bridges CPU-bound sync work into async contexts; no blocking calls directly on the tokio executor.

What zero-copy techniques did you use in Transmute?

Several. Cow<'_, DynamicImage> in PDF image downscaling — no heap copy when the image is already within the dimension limit.
